simulated_decision: Weak Accept as an internal method draft; Borderline for real AAAI submission
summary: The draft has moved from a sparse skeleton to a coherent experimental method paper. It now contains a clear problem framing, method name, mathematical objective, algorithmic procedure, architecture/configuration table, matched strict-750 results, qualitative grids, artifact diagnostics, destructive ablations, weight sweep findings, timing evidence, and explicit limitations. The key empirical claim is now properly bounded: the method is not raw-style SOTA, but provides a cleaner style-content trade-off than SaMST and avoids StyleID-like semantic drift.
strengths: Clear and defensible contribution: terminal SWD as style driver plus kinetic path regularization as content-preservation mechanism.
Main strict-750 table is concrete and uses complete local baselines only, avoiding overclaiming on smoke-tested methods.
Artifact-sensitive diagnostics directly address the SaMST failure mode instead of relying only on CLIP/LPIPS.
Destructive ablations are interpretable and support the claimed role of each major component.
Qualitative grid and zoom crops now give visual evidence beside the tables.
The paper explicitly states it is bridge-inspired rather than an exact Schrodinger Bridge solver, improving theoretical honesty.
remaining_blockers_for_real_aaai: The current PDF is compiled with a generic article template, not the official AAAI two-column author kit. This is a formatting blocker before submission.
The paper is 13 pages in the current one-column style; it will need aggressive compression/reallocation into main paper plus supplement.
Complete matched-protocol CAST, StyTr2, AesFA, and AesPA-Net runs are still missing. The current paper handles this honestly, but AAAI reviewers may still expect at least CAST/StyTr2 complete.
No user study is available. Because the SaMST argument depends partly on visual cleanliness/artifact preference, a small human study remains important.
Timing is not yet a fully controlled benchmark across all baselines, so efficiency claims must remain conservative.
AAAI policy around LLM-generated text is strict. This draft should be treated as an internal technical draft; authors must rewrite/verify final prose and ensure policy compliance.
next_iteration_plan: Create an AAAI-format or AAAI-ready compressed version once the desired target year author kit is fixed.
Move detailed metric explanations, extra ablation discussion, and long baseline status details to supplement.
Add a short human-study protocol section or placeholder only if data collection is actually planned.
If compute budget allows, prioritize complete strict-750 CAST and StyTr2 before adding more exotic baselines.
Audit references for exact venue/year/authors before submission.

acceptance_readiness.overall: not yet submission-ready, but now strong enough as a working paper draft
